messages:
Samir Gupta: Hey team — quick help please. My partner and I had our baby in Madrid while on a short work assignment. Hospital issued a receipt but Spanish civil registry is backlogged and we won't have a US birth certificate or passport for ~8 weeks. Can we add the baby to benefits now? Hospital is pushing an invoice.
Lina Morales: Congrats Samir! Short answer: yes we can provisionally enroll a dependent for emergency coverage, but we need documentation workflows for finalizing. Two parallel tracks: enrollment + claims coordination.
Samir Gupta: What docs can I upload now? I don't have a birth certificate or passport.
Lina Morales: Acceptable provisional docs:
- hospital discharge summary + official hospital invoice in the neonate's name, AND
- signed affidavit of parentage (notarized) OR pending registration receipt from Spanish registry, AND
- copy of parents' govt ID.
Upload PDFs to the benefits portal under "Dependent Docs - Intl". Use filename format: empID_lastname_newborn_country.pdf (e.g., 98765_Gupta_newborn_ES.pdf).
Samir Gupta: Ok uploading docs now. The hospital is threatening collections — any short-term paperwork I can show them?
Benefits Bot: Temporary proof-of-coverage letter generated (temp ID TRV-9876). This is valid for 21 days and states the newborn is provisionally enrolled pending final docs. Link: https://internal.benefits.redwood/portal/docs-download/TRV-9876
Travel Ops: For claims billed abroad, ask the provider to supply an itemized bill and the hospital's IBAN/SWIFT. We can attach the temporary letter when we contact the carrier to request direct billing or coordination. If the provider refuses, escalate to the local consulate for advice on medical billing enforcement.
Samir Gupta: Carrier contact? I assume BlueShield handles claims for international births?
Carrier Rep - BlueShield: Hi Samir — I'll open an international claims file. Please send the itemized invoice + temporary letter + any Spanish registry receipt. We'll assess eligibility for payment or reimbursement and advise on direct billing options. Expect initial reply in 48 hours.
Samir Gupta: Thanks — one more about premiums: will payroll charge dependent premiums immediately if we provisionally enroll?
Benefits Bot: Payroll policy: provisional enrollments put the dependent on benefits effective the hospital DOB for coverage purposes. Payroll will not charge until Benefits confirms the provisional enrollment in the system. If finalized retro to DOB, payroll will pro-rate premiums back to the DOB on the next run. Any refunds or additional deductions are posted as adjustments.
Lina Morales: I'll mark this as expedited due to active billing. Samir, can you DM me the scanned hospital invoice and the notarized affidavit? I will attach to the carrier ticket and to payroll.
Samir Gupta: DM'd both files and the registry receipt screenshot. Also, is there any special code or claim note we should include for foreign births?
Carrier Rep - BlueShield: Please include claim note: "INTL-BIRTH-NEO" and add the hospital invoice number. That helps route to the international claims unit. We'll also check Coordination of Benefits if the facility billed the mother or a local insurer.
Lina Morales: Noted. Samir — once BlueShield confirms, we'll issue a final confirmation email and upload the newborn to the benefits system. If everything finalizes, effective date = DOB and payroll retro applies.
Samir Gupta: Great — appreciate the fast help. If the consulate suggests a local payment hold, I'll loop Travel Ops. :thumbsup:
